hints: Because the resultant is perpendicular to the force $P$, the sum of components along the direction of $P$ must equal zero.
Resolve along the line of $P$: set $P + 5 \sin 60^\circ - 10 \sin 30^\circ = 0$ and solve for $P$.
Resolve perpendicular to the line of $P$: evaluate $Q = 10 \cos 30^\circ - 5 \cos 60^\circ$ to determine the magnitude of the resultant.
walkthrough: Choose an orthogonal coordinate system where the positive x-axis points in the direction of the force of magnitude $P$.

The problem states that the resultant of the three forces has magnitude $Q$ and is perpendicular to $P$. This means:
1. The x-component of the resultant is zero: $R_x = 0$.
2. The y-component of the resultant has magnitude $Q$: $|R_y| = Q$.

Step 1: Resolve all three forces along the direction of $P$ (x-axis):
- The force $P$ acts entirely along the positive x-axis: $P$.
- The $5\text{ N}$ force contributes a component: $+5 \sin 60^\circ$.
- The $10\text{ N}$ force contributes a component: $-10 \sin 30^\circ$.
Set the total x-component to zero:
$$R_x = P + 5 \sin 60^\circ - 10 \sin 30^\circ = 0$$

Substitute the trigonometric values $\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$ and $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866025$:
$$P + 5(0.866025) - 10(0.5) = 0$$
$$P + 4.330127 - 5 = 0$$
$$P = 5 - 4.330127 \approx 0.66987\text{ N} \approx 0.670\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Resolve all forces perpendicular to $P$ (y-axis):
- Force $P$ has no perpendicular component: $0$.
- The $10\text{ N}$ force has component: $+10 \cos 30^\circ$.
- The $5\text{ N}$ force has component: $-5 \cos 60^\circ$.
Set the total y-component equal to $Q$:
$$Q = 10 \cos 30^\circ - 5 \cos 60^\circ$$
